current_bounded_findings: Storage ownership must be explicit for a shared groundwater state.
Correct repartition of one physical storage is invariant; duplicate storage has a predictable signature.
A finite-resistance q-link is physically distinct from a shared-state h-link and from a storage tangent.
A shared groundwater head can be a valid shared variable without being a complete state descriptor of the unsaturated column.
Head-dependent ET and drain slopes are physical sink responses, not storage coefficients or interface conductances.
A local tangent can reproduce nonlinear integrated storage while remaining numerically distinct from the physical storage volume.
N:1 linear dummy-column aggregation is exactly area-weighted and permutation invariant.
Forcing order is irrelevant in the memoryless linear control but matters when an internal storage memory is retained, while total water remains conserved.
Fresh-simulation restart states must be transferred through exact model state rather than formatted text when conservation gates are tighter than input formatting precision.
Repeated external reanchoring inside one MODFLOW prepared solve is not equivalent to repeatedly solving fresh affine systems: nonlinear under-relaxation history can stall the head response.

After that history effect is removed, MODFLOW inner residual certification remains a separate acceptance layer; the physical root, external coupled residual and MODFLOW convergence certificate can close at different numerical thresholds.
